Miles, despite not having a scoring night, I thought he did a heck of a job defensively for us. There was a lot of contributions up and down the lineup and obviously we went with the guys that were playing well, they put us in a position to win. It was a tough, hard game, wish we could have come out with the win, but overall, just tremendous growth the last couple of games in my opinion.
clips.news_angle: Taylor Jenkins on team growth and Tyler's career-high performance

clips.video_title: Taylor Jenkins Postgame Press Conference | 11.21.26
clips.pull_quote: Tyler was phenomenal tonight, career high, Braden career high, but they made impacts in other ways.

clips.speaker: Taylor Jenkins
clips.text: He played just poised. He took what the defense gave him. He was being selective with his shots even though he scored 50, but his teammates did a great job getting him the ball. He was moving well without the ball. We started playing with a little bit more pace, I think that freed him up a little bit more. We dialed up some execution throughout the game, especially in the fourth quarter, which allowed him to have some big-time buckets. He just took where the space was and had great finishes, great shots. He was competing on defense, was getting offensive rebounds. Overall, this was just a great game by him. I just thought he played with great poise and confidence tonight.

They found the moments to both be aggressive and they were both in each other's ear even in the middle of the play, which I think really allowed them to find the playmaking opportunities throughout the game.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: We were down to the Clippers. He came in the locker room, he gave us all tools that day. He said, 'Turn that damn TV off. I don't want to watch no damn film.' He looked at that thing, ripped up the little practice paper, put it in the pocket. He said, 'No, look, he came in there, turn that damn TV off, I don't want to watch no damn film.'
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins recalls a heated practice session with the Clippers

clips.pull_quote: He looked at that thing, ripped up the little practice paper, put it in the pocket.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: Somebody came to the basket and Marc Gasol wasn't going to take the charge. It would have been a block, but Marc Gasol was about to take the charge and he jumps out of the way. I am pissed like crazy. After the game we come in the locker room and I said, 'Marc, I am disappointed, man.' I said, 'You had the chance to take a charge and you jumped out of the way.' Marc Gasol stopped and stood up. He said, 'What you trying to say, coach?' I stood there for a moment because I didn't have a second point. Finally I said, 'All I am trying to say is Mike Conley 175 pounds and Mike Conley took a charge and got crushed. You the biggest man out there.' And he went and sat down.
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins on Marc Gasol's refusal to take a charge
clips.social_post: Lionel Hollins recalls calling out Marc Gasol for refusing to take a charge: I told him Mike Conley is 175 pounds and took the hit, you are the biggest man out there.

clips.pull_quote: Mike Conley 175 pounds and Mike Conley took a charge and got crushed.

I said, 'There is a lot of stuff that you could write that would be good in terms of true, but it would just turn people off.' These guys aren't perfect and I don't expect them to be perfect. I can't tell them what to do or how to do. I can give my advice and tell them what I think, but they are all grown men. I try to help them become more mature.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: I never forget Kobe signed the deal for 130 plus million dollars. I'm at the press conference and it's actually a double press conference because they're introducing myself, Brian Grant, Lamar Odom to the city of Los Angeles. And then Kobe signed his deal and I never forget looking at that money. And then the first thing he turned to the right and said to me was, get ready to fucking black out. Get ready to work out. Let's take that shit to another level.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on Kobe Bryant's intense work ethic after signing his Lakers deal
clips.social_post: Caron Butler recalls the moment Kobe Bryant welcomed him to the Lakers with a clear message: get ready to work. Kobe told him to get ready to black out and take his game to another level.
clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: Get ready to fucking black out. Get ready to work out. Let's take that shit to another level.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: I never forget coming back from Antigua. I was doing a basketball without borders camp or clinic for the Miami Heat and the stroller was going across. This is like when everybody used to watch ESPN around the clock. I'm walking through the airport and they like, Shaquille O'Neal coming to the Miami Heat. I was like, damn, we about to be like dope. Leaving the Miami Heat and my name, they had Lamar Odom. I was like, oh shit, like that's how this work? I thought I was here forever. I just bought a crib. I can't sell my crib. It was just all that emotional attachment.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on Shaquille O'Neal's trade and the emotional impact on teammates
clips.social_post: Caron Butler opens up about the shock of being traded from the Heat for Shaquille ONeal. He had just bought a house and thought he was staying in Miami forever.
clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: I thought I was here forever. I just bought a crib. I can't sell my crib.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: Basketball genius. All he talked about was the game. I started watching film with him on every plane trip, just analyzing the rotations, the schemes, the double teams, where they was coming from, how to manipulate the defense. I learned a whole bunch from Kobe. And also too, when you talk about life after basketball, he gave me like a jewel that stuck with me. The roar of the crowd is not for you, it's for what you can do. And as soon as you can't do it, they be cheering for someone else. So work on your second act while you're in the midst of your first.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on Kobe Bryant's obsession with film study and game preparation
clips.social_post: Kobe Bryant gave Caron Butler some legendary life advice: The roar of the crowd is not for you, it is for what you can do. Work on your second act while you are in the midst of your first.
clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: I started watching film with him on every plane trip, just analyzing the rotations, the schemes.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: It's unique because I saw him literally put his guard down. I heard all these things about him before I got there like, don't fuck with him, he's selfish, he's this, he's that. And once I got there, the first thing I saw, he was just standing on business. So I was just like, I fuck with that. All he doing is he's standing on his business. And then I start asking him stuff and he like, man, sit right here, let's talk. And he just became like so welcoming.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on Kobe Bryant's business-focused personality off the court
clips.social_post: Caron Butler says the reputation of Kobe Bryant being selfish was wrong. Once he got to know him, he saw a guy who was just standing on business and was incredibly welcoming to his teammates.
clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: The first thing I saw, he was just standing on business.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: I told Lamar like, you want to come down, pull up? He like, all right, cool. He like, ask Kobe. Everybody was laughing like, he ain't coming. Like, Kobe, you want to come up, eat some ribs and shit and just kick it? He like, yeah, what time? I was like, laughing at them dudes like, see what I said? He came, he sat down, he kicked it with everybody. One of the most memorable moments of my life because the whole hood came out, the whole community. And he sat down, he ate with everybody, he just chopped it up, poured into them, gave them all life. That's just who he was.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on Kobe Bryant's connection with his community in Milwaukee
clips.social_post: Caron Butler shares a story of Kobe Bryant coming to his neighborhood to eat ribs and hang out with the community. It remains one of the most memorable moments of his life.
clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: One of the most memorable moments of my life because the whole hood came out.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: I was excited to go there because one, I watched that playoff series. I was in Chicago and I went to the game, Chicago playing the Wizards the year before with Larry Hughes and they had injuries but it was a hell of a battle. Gilbert hit the huge game winner to get them out that round in that series and I was just like, I want to be on that squad with Larry Hughes though. You know what I'm saying? Like I was just like, I can be on that and we was always talking about small ball and shit like that even in that era.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on joining the Wizards with Gilbert Arenas and Antawn Jamison
clips.social_post: Caron Butler reflects on his excitement to join the Wizards and play alongside Gilbert Arenas and Larry Hughes during their small ball era.
clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: I wanted to be on that squad with Larry Hughes though.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: He was one of the hardest workers. And I played with, obviously we talked about Kobe, I played with KD, played with Russell Westbrook, Chris Paul, obviously we shared that experience, Giannis, list of all the superstars out there. Gilbert is probably number two on that list behind Kobe obviously. But yeah, he top three hardest worker, dudes. Little quirky, but he has some shit to him but he was a dog when it came to that work and he had like a four-year stretch, maybe five, where nobody in the league wanted to see him coming. I mean, no team in the organization wanted to see him.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on Gilbert Arenas's work ethic and status as a superstar
clips.social_post: Caron Butler ranks Gilbert Arenas as the second hardest worker he ever played with, right behind Kobe Bryant. He says for a four or five year stretch, nobody in the league wanted to see him coming.
clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: He was a dog when it came to that work.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: This is when I knew LeBron was special. This all happened in one play. We played him three years in a row in the playoff series but this is when I knew he was special. We tried to go under on pick and rolls, that didn't work. We tried to go over, tried to bully over, we tried to shoot the gaps, we tried to stay connected, we tried to meet him in transition, tried everything. We tried to weak him, send the double team, late blacks. We showed him literally every coverage in the playoff series and he dissected it. And I was just like, he different. That's when I knew. As long as he stayed available and durable, he's going to probably shatter just about every record.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on the Wizards' defensive strategy against LeBron James
clips.social_post: Caron Butler says he knew LeBron James was special when the Wizards tried every defensive coverage against him in the playoffs and he dissected all of them.
clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: We showed him literally every coverage in the playoff series and he dissected it.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: It was dope because I think as players, obviously we have a checkbox of our own like when we come into the league. One, whether people like it or not, you want to be a household name. You want to be respected by your peers, you want to get the bag, you want to be an All-Star, you want to get a chip, and you want to get the hell out. That's the checklist that all of us have as players, as competitive players. And I was able to check one of those things by making an All-Star team.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on the competitive checklist for NBA players
clips.social_post: Caron Butler breaks down the competitive checklist for NBA players: be a household name, get respected by peers, get the bag, be an All Star, win a chip, and get out.
clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: Whether people like it or not, you want to be a household name.

clips.speaker: Caron Butler
clips.text: My best year was pretty much, even though I was an isolation player, it came from being with great teammates. Gilbert made sure I was successful, Antawn made sure I was successful. I played in the Princeton offense, getting 21 a game that season. So that's not easy. Like the ball finds energy and it found me. So it was a dope experience.
clips.news_angle: Caron Butler on the importance of teammates like Gilbert Arenas and Antawn Jamison

clips.video_title: Caron Butler Reveals the Side of Kobe Bryant Nobody Saw
clips.pull_quote: Gilbert made sure I was successful, Antawn made sure I was successful.

clips.speaker: Chris Mannix

He's just figured some stuff out and he's coming into his own as a playmaker in this league.

clips.social_post: Evan Turner highlights Davion Mitchell's defensive impact, noting how he acts as the head of the snake by disrupting opposing emotional leaders like Fred VanVleet to force teams to crack.

clips.pull_quote: he was able to disrupt some of their emotional leaders.

clips.text: I keyed in before the season on the three-point shooting with Miami. You've got Larsen shooting 47%, you got Mitchell shooting close to 44%, you got Clay Thompson at 43%. You got guys that are making three-point shots and I mentioned Wiggins, he's not played well this season, there's still hope I'm sure there that he can improve his play. They've figured some stuff out too as well. I think for me, just like I talked about the top with Walker Kessler being like the wildcard with the Lakers going from good to great, I think the same thing about Davion Mitchell. I think you know what you're going to get from Giannis, you know what you're going to get from Bam, Clay may not be Warriors Clay, but he's still a pretty good player. If Mitchell can like play other point guards to like a standstill, they're good.

clips.speaker: Penny Hardaway
clips.text: When you're a former NBA player, you get a lot of flak coming in, especially the way that I did. I came in with no experience and got a head coaching job, so a lot of guys didn't look upon that as being great. Everything that we do as former NBA players on this level, it has to be heightened to the 100th power, honestly, because everything that we're not doing as what a normal college coach would do is going to get frowned upon. So for me, every year, I have the hardest non-conference schedule to try to prove myself as a coach, to try to go out and get a group of young men that are going to believe in and buy in.

I take them pretty serious because you know as well as anything to go eight and zero on a road with a young team, that's legit. Even though obviously the teams haven't been as sexy, they show up. I think they've been able to cut off a couple of months because they've been in their development because they've been able to build an identity. They compete, they play ten deep. One thing that we bring up on Cam Boozer, he's playing far beyond his years. Not only is this a good playmaker, a good passer, a solid scorer, but he reads the game so efficiently and he has size to him.

clips.text: One of the most remarkable things about the Grizzlies is that they've got 15 guys averaging 10 or more minutes per game. Nobody is playing more than 31 minutes per game. Only Scotty Pippen Jr. has played five or less games. Everybody else has played more than nine games. Everybody else has played more than half the season on this team. They've taken some heat for how they've deconstructed the roster, and it's been painful over the years. Desmond Bane is gone, Jaren Jackson Jr. is gone, Ja Morant, the last one to go. But they did that to create a roster that was built for the Taylor Jenkins style of play. This guy comes from that European culture. He wants to play a whole bunch of guys, he wants to play a free-flowing offense, he wants the ball to move, and they are playing that way.

And here you go again, where they plucked Ty Jerome, who is not a celebrated signing when they got him a couple of years ago, but a good one. Zach Edey was a back half of the lottery guy, they nailed that. Jaylen Wells, they nailed that pick. Cam Spencer, they develop him up until this point.
